subject: Pilot padding: voucher credit vs. short extension — procurement constraints
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cobalthealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC runway — need quick decision on padding (voucher vs short extension)

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from our side — we hit a higher-than-expected model burn during last week's integration tests and our internal compliance team needs either: (A) a 21-day extension on the timeboxed POC, or (B) a one-time voucher/credit that covers the excess usage so we can stay within the originally scoped dates.

Procurement prefers vouchers to avoid amendment paperwork, but Legal says any credit that affects invoicing needs sign-off. We're on a tight window: if we don't lock something before next Friday we risk delaying our internal demo.

I've attached the current PO (Cobalt_PO_4321.pdf) and a quick burn report (POC_metrics.xlsx). Can you outline what Redwood can do here — short-term extension terms and a voucher amount estimate? Also include any implications for SLA/priority in case we push traffic.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of AI Integrations, Cobalt Health
[Attachment: Cobalt_PO_4321.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: POC_metrics.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway — need quick decision on padding (voucher vs short extension)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the data and the PO. Quick summary of options from our side: 

1) 21-day timebox extension (same rate) — we can do this as an amendment to the POC SOW; requires signature from procurement & legal on both sides. Lead time: 2–3 business days for internal approvals. No price change; SLA/priority remains as-is.

2) One-time voucher/credit to cover overage — simplest from procurement perspective. We can issue a voucher equal to the measured overage (we reviewed POC_metrics.xlsx). For this customer size and potential conversion, I can offer a voucher covering 80% of the overage up to a cap of $9,000. This can be processed as a credit memo applied to the next invoice.

3) Hybrid — small 7–10 day extension plus a reduced voucher for residual overage. This minimizes contract churn while giving you runway for the demo.

Notes on SLA/priority: short extensions do not change routing tiers; if you expect bursty production-like traffic we can temporarily bump the priority tier for the POC at a nominal uplift (typically adds 12% on a short amendment). We only enable priority bump with explicit approval because it affects capacity allocations.

I'll loop Marcus (finance) and David (account exec) to run the voucher accounting and expedite the amendment paperwork if you prefer the extension. Which option would Procurement sign off on fastest?

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Healthcare & Life Sciences
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Cobalt_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, Elaine Park <elaine@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway — need quick decision on padding (voucher vs short extension)

Kim / Elaine — finance POV: voucher is simplest operationally. A credit memo against the next invoice avoids amending the SOW and is typically acceptable to procurement (per Elaine's note). A couple of constraints: 

- Voucher applied as credit memo must be recognized in the same fiscal quarter as the invoice it offsets.
- If Cobalt wants the voucher to appear as a vendor discount on the PO we will need a short acknowledgement email from procurement confirming intent (this avoids reclassifying revenue).
- For the 80% voucher cap Kim suggested — we can make it 85% if Marketing/RevOps is comfortable; otherwise $9k cap stands.

If Procurement needs zero paperwork, propose: Redwood issues credit memo for $7,500 (net) which Procurement applies to next invoice and sends us a short confirmation email (1–2 lines). That gets you demo runway and keeps legal churn low.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procurement@cobalthealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway — need quick decision on padding (voucher vs short extension)

Hi all — procurement here. Elaine and Legal conferred: voucher preferred. We cannot add amendments to the PO after the fact without a further approval step that will take >7 business days. If Redwood can issue a $7,500 credit memo and provide a one-line acknowledgment (we buy it as ‘vendor credit for POC overage’), we will apply it against upcoming invoices and can confirm internally the demo schedule will stay the same.

For audit trail, please include the original PO number (PO 4321) on the credit memo and the accompanying email.

Regards,
Alicia Gonzalez
Lead, Strategic Procurement — Cobalt Health
[Attachment: Cobalt_PO_4321.pdf (pdf)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement <procurement@cobalthealth.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway — need quick decision on padding (voucher vs short extension)

Alicia / Elaine — thank you. We will issue the $7,500 credit memo today and reference PO 4321 in the memo and email. Marcus — can finance route the credit and share a PDF of the memo to procurement and Elaine?

Next steps / acceptance criteria:
- Redwood issues credit memo $7,500 referencing PO 4321 (today).
- Procurement confirms receipt by reply (one-line email acceptable).
- Elaine signs off that the demo date is unchanged; Redwood will monitor the POC traffic and raise a priority-bump request if you plan sustained production-like bursts.

I'll follow up after finance shares the memo.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Healthcare & Life Sciences
Redwood Inference
